evidence.observation: The class under contract. Its constructor is overloaded: with a MetadataClientConfig it builds a V3HttpTransport (after throwing ParamError for a missing apiKey/serviceId, lines 122-123); with a Transport-shaped object (`"post" in configOrTransport`, line 118) it accepts an injected transport. Every /v3/meta/* method is a thin `this.http.post(...)` delegation, so the client's failure surface is exactly {ParamError for local validation} U {TDAMError produced by the transport}; no method returns or throws a raw response shape.

Normalizes every metadata request payload (stripUndefined) and rejects non-object payloads with `new ParamError("request payload must be an object")`. Because it is called synchronously inside each method (e.g. `createUser(p)`, line 136) before `http.post` runs, a bad payload produces a typed ParamError and never reaches the wire.

Operation-scoped precondition helper: if none of the listed fields is a non-empty string it throws `ParamError("<operation> requires one of <fields>")`. It gives metadata callers a stable, typed and self-describing failure (name + operation + accepted fields) instead of a generic TypeError or a server round-trip.

Representative validated metadata operation: the overloads normalize the (string | request) argument through the module-level `body()` helper and then call `requireAnyString(payload, ["user_id", "user_key"], "listTeams")` (line 187) before posting to /v3/meta/team/list. An under-specified call therefore fails as a typed ParamError without any HTTP request, which demo case 8 asserts.

Same contract for tasks: `requireAnyString(payload, ["team_id", "creator_user_id", "creator_user_key"], "listTasks")` (line 224). Together with listTeams it shows the validation failure is uniform across the metadata surface, so a caller can catch `ParamError` rather than inspecting a raw payload/response object.

Success and failure plumbing for the read path used by the demo: a string or GetUserRequest is folded into a body and posted to /v3/meta/user/get; on success the resolved value is the unwrapped `data` payload, on failure the rejection is whatever typed error the transport raised (TDAMError) — the envelope itself is never returned.

Posted with `{ user_key }` only. Used by demo case 6, where the gateway answers HTTP 401 with an envelope carrying `code: 0`; the client still fails with a typed TDAMError whose code falls back to the HTTP status (401) rather than resolving a bogus body.
Zero-argument metadata call (body `{}`) used by demo case 4: an HTTP 200 whose body is not JSON is still rejected as a typed TDAMError (sentinel code -1) instead of leaking a raw string.

The single normalizer every v3 client (metadata, prompt, skill, generation-log) shares. Its constructor rejects malformed configuration with ParamError, and `post`/`get` funnel into `request`, which is where HTTP- and envelope-level failures are converted into typed errors.

The normalization algorithm the contract pins down: (a) a body that fails JSON.parse becomes TDAMError with code `-1` on a 2xx (line 91) or the HTTP status otherwise, and the raw text only appears inside the normalized message; (b) when `!response.ok || businessCode !== 0` the error code is the business code when non-zero else the HTTP status (line 99), requestId prefers x-qcloud-transaction-id then x-trace-id then envelope.request_id (lines 81-84, 107), and envelope `data` objects are narrowed into `details` (lines 100-103); (c) on success only `envelope.data` plus `trace_id` is returned (lines 112-117), so no envelope keys leak.

The typed remote-failure shape: a real Error subclass named "TDAMError" exposing numeric `code`, string `requestId`, and optional `details` (documented as server diagnostics preserved for recovery). Its message is normalized as `[<code>] <message> (request_id=<id>)`, which is what the demo asserts instead of any raw response shape.

The typed local-failure shape: a TypeError subclass named "ParamError", so callers can distinguish bad input/configuration (`instanceof ParamError`, also `instanceof TypeError`) from remote failures (`instanceof TDAMError`) without parsing messages or inspecting raw objects.

The sibling metadata/prompt client. It has its own typed preconditions (`requireText`, `requireTarget`, lines 30-39) throwing ParamError and delegates to the same Transport/V3HttpTransport; demo case 9 shows its server-side failures arrive as the same TDAMError shape, confirming the contracted behavior is a client-wide invariant rather than metadata-only.

claims.claim: The metadata client's failure surface is closed under two typed SDK errors: remote/response failures surface as TDAMError (Error subclass with numeric code, string requestId, normalized message, narrowed optional details) and local validation/configuration failures surface as ParamError (TypeError subclass named "ParamError"). A caller can therefore branch on `instanceof` and never has to inspect a raw Response, raw body string, or bare { code, message } envelope.

Metadata payload validation is fail-fast and typed: `body()` throws ParamError("request payload must be an object") for non-object payloads and `requireAnyString()` throws ParamError("<operation> requires one of <fields>") for under-specified list calls, both synchronously before `http.post` is invoked, so demo case 8 observes ParamError with zero HTTP requests issued.

Every /v3/meta/* call inherits the V3HttpTransport normalization: a non-zero envelope business code wins over the HTTP status, the HTTP status is used when the envelope code is 0/non-numeric, a non-JSON body becomes TDAMError with sentinel code -1 on a 2xx and the HTTP status otherwise, and the request id is folded from x-qcloud-transaction-id / x-trace-id / envelope.request_id into TDAMError.requestId.

Diagnostics returned by the gateway inside the error envelope's `data` field are preserved as a narrowed `details` object (e.g. `{ current_version: 7 }` for a stale-version conflict) rather than exposing the whole envelope, so conflict recovery code reads typed fields instead of a raw response shape.

MetadataClient accepts an injected Transport (`"post" in configOrTransport` constructor overload), and a TDAMError raised by that transport propagates to the caller unchanged (identity preserved), i.e. typed failures are never re-wrapped or re-shaped by the client methods.

The contract is not metadata-only: the sibling MemoryPromptClient uses its own ParamError preconditions and the same V3HttpTransport, so a prompt-client server failure (`code: 42007`) arrives as the same normalized TDAMError, while the success path unwraps `data` (plus `trace_id`) and never exposes envelope keys.

conclusion: Contracted: the v3 MetadataClient (repository tdam) exposes a typed, normalized failure surface instead of leaking raw response shapes. Remote failures reach the caller as TDAMError instances (numeric `code` derived from the envelope business code or the HTTP status, `requestId` folded from the transport headers/correlating envelope field, message normalized as `[code] message (request_id=...)`, optional `details` narrowed to the envelope's diagnostic `data`) and local failures as ParamError instances (a TypeError subclass) raised synchronously before any request is sent. Non-JSON bodies, HTTP-200-with-code-0 gateway answers and conflict payloads all funnel through the same V3HttpTransport normalizer, and an injected transport's typed error is passed through unchanged. Evidence for the contract is the executable demo .prale-eval/metadata-client-failure.contract.mjs (10/10 cases passing over the unmodified sources) plus the cited symbols; no repository source file, task metadata, lockfile or git configuration was modified.

validation.notes: 10/10 cases pass (metadata failure: envelope business code -> TDAMError 41002 with header requestId; envelope request_id fallback 50003; non-JSON 502 body -> TDAMError with numeric code 502; HTTP 200 non-JSON -> sentinel code -1; conflict diagnostics preserved as details {current_version: 7}; HTTP-401 + envelope code 0 -> code 401; success control unwraps data and does not leak the envelope; local validation -> ParamError (TypeError subclass) for createUser(undefined)/listTeams({})/listTasks({})/missing apiKey with zero fetch calls; prompt client failure -> same TDAMError shape; injected transport TDAMError propagates by identity). The demo loads the real TypeScript sources through Node's built-in type stripping via .prale-eval/harness/loader.mjs, which (a) maps the SDK's `./x.js` specifiers to `./x.ts` and (b) substitutes .prale-eval/harness/undici-shim.mjs because the declared runtime dependency `undici` (imported by src/v3/http.ts) is NOT installed in this offline workspace and no dependency installation was permitted; the TLS-relaxing Agent is never constructed by the demo. No network access is used: globalThis.fetch is stubbed. Limitation: the repository's own suite runner is vitest (`npm test` -> `vitest run`, devDependency) and it is unavailable offline (no node_modules), so the vendored vitest suite could not be executed; the equivalent contract was executed with Node's built-in test runner instead. A supporting citation check (`node .prale-eval/validate-evidence.mjs`) re-verifies that every evidence path exists and that each cited symbol really occurs inside its inclusive start_line/end_line range.
